note: Single source of truth for the fixed GOAL. Edit numbers here: the latency model, the reports viewer, and the converter all read this file. Durations are nanoseconds. block_count is how many block times the transaction path spans (a per-phase consensus plan). The E2E formula follows the transaction lifecycle: E2E = network_rtt_ns/2 (client request -> RPC; the submission response is off the critical path, so only half the round trip counts) + send_tx_p99_ns (in-RPC sendTransaction handler) + block_count*block_time_ns (consensus) + ingest_p99_target_ns (meta available -> ingested in RPC) + network_rtt_ns (getTransaction request + response round trip) + get_tx_p99_ns (in-RPC getTransaction handler). No slice depends on a measured client<->RPC network time: the network legs are hardcoded constants from the assumed 50 ms round trip. A phase that omits ingest_p99_target_ns has it derived from the E2E budget: e2e_budget_ns - block_count*block_time_ns - (3*network_rtt_ns/2 + send_tx_p99_ns + get_tx_p99_ns).
query_load_note: Open-loop query load model, derived 2026-09-01. Two families of requirement, judged and reported separately — never folded into one verdict. Full derivation: docs/sla-derivation.md. (1) sla: every endpoint runs at its share of the team RPC SLA doc's Standard-tier sustained watermark (section 3.4: 500 rps aggregate on one node, mix txhash 0.60 / events 0.20 / txpage 0.15 / ledgers 0.05) and answers for the p99 of section 4.1. The floors are a property of the endpoint alone, so they are the same in every phase and every dataset profile, and they are stored once. p99_ns is keyed by endpoint then storage tier, and the tier keys are the SLA's data-age windows: hot = Live, cold = Recent (frozen-NVMe). The third window, Historical (frozen-EBS), is out of scope — the benchmark boxes carry no EBS tier. (2) e2e_probe: getTransaction ALSO runs at the demand-derived floors of work item 856, per profile and per phase, and answers only for in_rpc_p99_ns, its slice of the end-to-end transaction-lifecycle budget in fixed_estimates. The scheduled p99 of that cell is reported, never judged. Load is an arrival rate, not a concurrency level: each leg is paced at ladder x floor (0.5x/1x/2x) and the verdict cell is 1x. For the sla family the ladder IS the doc's tier set: 0.5x = Light (250 rps aggregate), 1x = Standard (500), 2x = Heavy (1000). getTransaction therefore sweeps ONE leg carrying both ladders, deduped and sorted ascending; where the two floors coincide the shared cell carries both verdicts. Profiles are keyed by dataset model name (the dataset name with its per-ledger tx count stripped: sac-6000 -> sac). e2e_probe.floors_rps arrays are indexed by phase: [phase 1, phase 2, phase 3]. A leg drives one endpoint at a time, so the mix rates apply per endpoint in sequence, not as one blended 500 rps stream.
